docs.text: FACIS Zero Trust Demonstrator ¶ This is the documentation for the FACIS Zero Trust Demonstrator (FACIS.ZTD), an Apache-2.0 demonstrator released inside the Eclipse XFSC organisation. The demonstrator stands up two demonstration zones and lets a participant backend in one zone call a protected resource in the other, with every hop authenticated, authorised and attested. It is built to show the refusals as clearly as the successes: a revoked credential, a wrong scope or a tampered measurement each produce a distinct, explained denial. Where to start ¶ If you want to Read Understand what the demonstrator does Features and journeys Drive it and read what it tells you Using the demonstrator Stand it up or tear it down Deployment Set up a specific cluster step by step Environments Know how it is built and shipped Packaging and containers Follow the orchestrated journeys Orchestrated flows Wire up identity Keycloak integration Call its APIs API documentation See how acceptance is proven BDD acceptance and the BDD catalogue of every Annex A row Understand the pipeline CI/CD Diagnose a problem Troubleshooting Check what it depends on OSS dependencies and Licenses Find where we depart from the specification Specification changes Understand why it is built this way Architecture decisions , including how the TDR decisions ADR 001–006 are applied Conventions this documentation follows ¶ Documentation follows the Eclipse Project Handbook : everything a contributor or user needs lives in this repository, in Markdown, under docs/ or in the README, and is published from the same commit as the code it describes. The FAP Partner Onboarding project is the reference for structure — its specification and its implementation — so a reader who knows one FACIS repository can navigate this one without relearning where things are. How the project applies the handbook's contribution, intellectual-property and release rules is in CONTRIBUTING.md . The site is built with MkDocs and published to GitHub Pages on every change to main . Project context ¶ FACIS.ZTD is delivered for the FACIS project and published in Eclipse XFSC. The wider FACIS programme — Federation Architecture Patterns, machine-readable SLAs, digital contracting and the other demonstrators — is indexed at eclipse-xfsc/facis . Licence ¶ Apache License 2.0. docs.text: API documentation ¶ Interface registry ¶ The demonstrator's cross-component interfaces are identified IF-01 through IF-08 . Version 1 of each is defined by the machine-readable artefacts in docs/contracts/ , which CI validates on every change (see Validation ). A v1 contract changes only by a compatible addition; anything else is a v2. Interface Purpose v1 artefacts Status IF-01 Security-state event stream to the demonstrator UI event , snapshot , feed API v1 IF-02 Connector authorization surface — registration and token issuance connector API v1 IF-03 Credential verification outcome JWS payload , JWS header , signing rules v1 IF-04 Observability and evidence The IF-01 event schema, as a JSON log line; rules v1 IF-05 Policy decision input and output input , decision , header rules v1 IF-06 Governed configuration change change v1 IF-07 Attested channel control States and rules v0, not frozen IF-08 Scenario driver hooks lifecycle command , lifecycle result v1 (delivered with the BDD pack) Internal to a zone, and not a numbered interface: the token store's API, token-store.v1.openapi.yaml — substitution for the guard and DPoP replay detection for the connector and the guard. Three agreements are conventions rather than interfaces, and are documented where they live: Convention Where Identity provider realm, clients, roles and scopes Keycloak integration Repository, CI and Helm conventions CI/CD , Packaging and containers Acceptance evidence and its handover BDD acceptance Upstream APIs are referenced and pinned, never redefined here: Envoy ext_authz ( envoy/service/auth/v3 ), Keycloak OIDC, SPIFFE Workload API, the attested-TLS library, and the XFSC services' own APIs. Reason codes ¶ Every refusal names a code from one registry, reason-codes.json (schema: reason-codes.v1.schema.json ). A family names the layer that refuses, its default HTTP status and the state the UI shows; a code may override the status. Family Layer Default HTTP UI state Overrides ADM admission 403 BLOCKED-ADMISSION — MESH identity and mesh policy none (connection refused) BLOCKED-IDENTITY — TOK token authentication 401 DENIED-TOKEN TOK-SCOPE 403, TOK-REQUEST-INVALID 400, TOK-REGISTRATION-REJECTED 400, TOK-NO-UPSTREAM 409, TOK-CALLER-DENIED 403, TOK-ROUTE-DENIED 403, TOK-STORE-UNAVAILABLE 503, TOK-SERVER-ERROR 500 POL policy decision 403 DENIED-POLICY POL-PRESENTATION-REQUIRED 401, POL-PDP-UNAVAILABLE 503, POL-BUNDLE-STALE 503 CRED credential verification 403 DENIED-CREDENTIAL — CHAN attested channel none (handshake refused) CHANNEL-DOWN — CFG configuration governance 422 CHANGE-REJECTED CFG-NOT-AUTHORISED 403 VIS display none (display state) UNKNOWN — The status is what a protected resource — the guard — returns to its caller. Two surfaces keep statuses of their own: the connector's token and registration endpoints answer with the OAuth 2.0 statuses (400 for a DPoP proof or nonce problem at the token endpoint, for example; see IF-02 ), and the token store's internal API states its own; the guard maps both to the caller's refusal. Admission refusals, one code per cause: ADM-UNSIGNED , ADM-NO-ATTESTATION , ADM-ATTESTATION-INVALID , ADM-SBOM-MISSING , ADM-SBOM-INVALID , ADM-NOT-LINUX , ADM-ARCH-UNSUPPORTED (only linux/amd64 is admitted), ADM-INDEX-UNSUPPORTED (only single-platform manifests are admitted), ADM-NOT-DIGEST , ADM-REGISTRY-DENIED , ADM-NAME-INVALID , and ADM-PROVIDER-DOWN when verification cannot run — admission then fails closed. Mapping of existing vocabularies ¶ The connector's error responses carry the OAuth 2.0 members plus a reason member ( Connector OAuth2 provider ). They map one to one onto the registry's codes; the HTTP status stays the connector's: Connector reason Registry code invalid_request TOK-REQUEST-INVALID invalid_client TOK-CLIENT-INVALID invalid_token TOK-INVALID ( TOK-MISSING when no token was presented) insufficient_scope TOK-SCOPE registration_rejected TOK-REGISTRATION-REJECTED server_error TOK-SERVER-ERROR dpop_invalid_proof TOK-PROOF-INVALID dpop_replayed TOK-REPLAY dpop_use_nonce TOK-NONCE dpop_jkt_mismatch TOK-JKT-MISMATCH dpop_invalid_ath TOK-ATH-MISMATCH IF-08 keeps the errors.action vocabulary it was delivered with (below); it reports the outcome of an operator command, not an access refusal, so it is not part of the registry. IF-01 — security-state feed ¶ Components write IF-01 events as JSON log lines. A feed bridge collects them per run and serves the UI a snapshot followed by a server-sent event stream; WebSocket is not used, since the flow is one way. Order and delivery. Ordering holds per source only; across sources, events are ordered for display by ts and correlation_id . Delivery is at least once and the UI deduplicates by (run_id, seq) . Staleness. On a sequence gap or a stale ts a panel shows UNKNOWN , never its last known value. When the bridge's buffer of 1000 events per run overflows, it drops the oldest and emits a gap event with VIS-STALE . On reconnect the UI reads the snapshot and resumes from as_of_seq + 1 . Content. A decision or admission event is allowed or denied , and a denial names its reason code. Events carry no secrets or tokens; detail is at most 512 characters. IF-03 — signed verification outcome ¶ The verification service signs the outcome of an OID4VP presentation check; the connector's issuance consumes it. The outcome is an object, never a boolean. Format. A compact JWS (RFC 7515). The payload is the UTF-8 JSON of if03-verification-outcome.v1.schema.json . The protected header has exactly alg , kid and typ ( if03-jws-header.v1.schema.json ): alg is ES256 , typ is facis-verification-outcome+jws . Any other member — crit , b64 , jwk , jku , x5u , x5c — is refused, so a key or a processing rule is never taken from the token itself. Key selection. The verifier holds a configured set of trusted issuers, each with its keys. kid selects one key; the payload's iss must be the issuer that key belongs to. An unknown kid , a key of another issuer, or a signature that does not verify → CRED-OUTCOME-SIGNATURE . Consumption. An outcome is consumed only when all hold, otherwise the grant is refused with the code named: status is verified → else CRED-OUTCOME-NOT-VERIFIED ; client_id , challenge and audience equal those of the grant request → else CRED-OUTCOME-MISMATCH ; the validity interval is sound and current: verified_at is before expires_at , at most 120 s before it, and not more than 30 s in the future (clock skew); now is before expires_at → else CRED-OUTCOME-EXPIRED ; outcome_id has not been consumed before; it is recorded in the same transaction that issues the grant → else CRED-OUTCOME-CONSUMED . A failed or revoked outcome carries its CRED-* reason; a verified one carries none. IF-04 — observability and evidence ¶ Every component logs JSON to stdout; security-relevant events use the IF-01 event schema, so the same record feeds the UI, the collector and the acceptance evidence. correlation_id is the guard's x-request-id (see the header rules below) and joins the events of one request across components; W3C trace context ( traceparent ) links the spans. Acceptance evidence — reports, logs and the manifest — is described in BDD acceptance . Header propagation, guard to gateway ¶ The guard terminates the caller's TLS, authenticates the caller's DPoP-bound token, asks the policy engine (IF-05), and forwards an allowed request towards the zone's gateway. What it forwards: Header Rule Authorization , DPoP Removed from the caller's request after verification. With the substitute_upstream_token obligation they are replaced by the token store's values: the upstream token, and a new proof minted with the store's key for exactly the upstream method and URI. The caller's proof is never forwarded. Without a successful substitution the request is refused, not forwarded. DPoP-Nonce Not relayed to the caller. When the upstream answers with a nonce challenge, the guard asks the token store once more with that nonce ( upstream_nonce ) and retries with the new proof; a second challenge is a refusal. X-Forwarded-For , X-Forwarded-Proto , X-Forwarded-Host , Forwarded Removed when they arrive from outside the mesh. Only the mesh ingress sets them. The proof's htu is rebuilt from configuration — https://<published host><route path> — never from these headers or Host . x-request-id Generated by the guard for a request from outside the mesh (an inbound value is replaced), then carried unchanged. It is the correlation_id of IF-01, IF-04 and IF-05. traceparent , tracestate Propagated (W3C Trace Context). Any x-facis-* header Removed from the caller's request; only the guard sets them. IF-07 — attested channel control ¶ Not frozen: the channel's control surface is defined by the attested-channel component when it is built. What is fixed now: States: connecting → handshake → attested → draining → closed , with error edges to refused (carrying a CHAN-* code) and lost . These are the state values of IF-01 channel_state events. Rules: the evidence is bound to one TLS session, so a channel has a maximum lifetime and is replaced by a freshly attested one rather than refreshed. The gateway port speaks only the attested protocol; a plain TLS or plaintext client is refused ( CHAN-DOWNGRADE ). Attestation evidence ¶ The mock attestation document — what a Trusted Execution Environment would emit, produced in software because the demonstrator has no TEE hardware — is described by contracts/mock-attestation.schema.json , with one sample per vendor profile in contracts/samples/ . It is a single format serving both sides of the evidence path: the artefact attached to a release and verified at admission, and the report exchanged inside the attested channel. It therefore underlies both IF-04 and IF-07. IF-04 is already frozen at v1 with the IF-01 event schema as its contract, so this format is not part of it; whether IF-07 carries it as its own contract is settled when IF-07 is frozen. IF-08 — deployment lifecycle command ¶ The scenario driver hook that deploys and uninstalls a release through the ORCE workflow. It is what the lifecycle acceptance scenarios (TDR-BDD-01..04) drive, and it is the same workflow an operator uses. Command: POST /lifecycle on ORCE, HTTP Basic ( httpNodeAuth ), TLS 1.3, management plane only — OpenAPI definition . The answer comes at once: 202 with data.accepted , or 400 with errors.fields naming each invalid parameter. Result: asynchronous, kept in the ORCE flow context under lifecycle.jobs[requestId] — JSON Schema . Read it with the ORCE admin API, GET /context/flow/ztd-lifecycle-tab/lifecycle , using a read-only bearer token. Reason codes ( errors.action ): valuesSchemaRejected , dryRunRejected , deployFailed , uninstallFailed , releaseNotFound , clusterUnreachable , duplicateRequest , invalidAction , systemError . A parameter the cluster refuses (for example a namespace outside the BDD pool) comes back in errors.fields . Validation ¶ npm run contracts (and the Contracts CI job) checks that: every JSON Schema compiles as strict JSON Schema 2020-12 and its $id carries v1 ; under contracts/fixtures/<schema>/ , every valid-* fixture passes and every invalid-* fixture fails, and each schema has at least one of each; the registry is well formed, every code sits in its family, and every reason code used in a fixture, an OpenAPI document or this page is registered; every OpenAPI document parses without duplicate keys, validates against the official OpenAPI 3.1 schema (vendored with its checksum), resolves every reference, and every Schema Object in it compiles as strict JSON Schema 2020-12. Conventions ¶ REST APIs are described with OpenAPI 3.1 (IF-08, delivered earlier, with OpenAPI 3.0); events and stored objects with JSON Schema 2020-12. Structured data carries a JSON-LD context and a SHACL shape where the content is meant to be interoperable rather than internal. Error responses use the shared reason-code registry, so a refusal is machine-readable and not just a status code.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ 6. Plane separation and staleness windows ¶ Trust boundaries (diagram 03) ¶ Each trust zone is its own SPIFFE trust domain. The two domains meet only through the attested channel and a TRAIN verdict; they are never merged. Data-plane calls into the management plane are denied by default, and a workload without an SVID or running an unsigned image cannot join or start. Source: diagrams/03-trust-boundaries.mmd . Allow matrix (data plane → management plane) ¶ Default DENY at both layers (NetworkPolicy and mesh AuthorizationPolicy). These are the only permitted paths: From data-plane workload → Allowed? Path/layer that enforces PDP adapter → TSA policy engine ALLOW (mTLS, named pair) mesh policy aTLS gateway → cmcd / TCR resolve ALLOW (named pair) mesh policy workloads → OTel collector (export only) ALLOW (declared bypass, ZT-26) mesh policy, egress-restricted workloads → DNS ALLOW (declared bypass) NetworkPolicy port 53 anything else data → management (SPIRE server, ArgoCD, OpenBao, TSPA, Harbor, estserver, admin APIs) DENY both layers; ZT-55 matrix test Staleness matrix ¶ Maximum window in which a revoked or rotated artefact still authorises. All values are proposed. Artefact Rotation/lifetime Cache Max stale-authorisation window SVID 1 h TTL in-process ≤ 1 h (mesh) Keycloak/issuer JWKS rotate on demand guard cache 5 min ≤ 5 min Access token 300 s lifetime — ≤ 300 s after revocation of its basis Policy bundle poll 60 s TSA cache ≤ 60 s Trust list / measurement TTL 300 s TCR/gateway ≤ 300 s + channel lifetime 15 min ⇒ ≤ ~20 min for an established channel (bounded by channel re-establishment) Credential revocation checked per verification outcome TTL 120 s ≤ renewal interval (≤ token lifetime 300 s) + 120 s

Artefact Rotation/lifetime Cache Max stale-authorisation window SVID 1 h TTL in-process ≤ 1 h (mesh) Keycloak/issuer JWKS rotate on demand guard cache 5 min ≤ 5 min Access token 300 s lifetime — ≤ 300 s after revocation of its basis Policy bundle poll 60 s TSA cache ≤ 60 s Trust list / measurement TTL 300 s TCR/gateway ≤ 300 s + channel lifetime 15 min ⇒ ≤ ~20 min for an established channel (bounded by channel re-establishment) Credential revocation checked per verification outcome TTL 120 s ≤ renewal interval (≤ token lifetime 300 s) + 120 s

How rows are run and reported is described in BDD acceptance . implemented : the scenario has real steps and decides the row. pending : the scenario is the Annex wording with pending steps; it runs, is reported as not run , and proves nothing yet. Evidence basis : what a run's evidence was produced with, read from the run itself. This page is built from the repository, not from a run: each cluster run publishes its own copy of the catalogue with the basis filled in. 94 rows: 8 implemented, 86 pending. Report G7 pending Cucumber.js ZT-01 — Secure Service Mesh ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-001 Acceptance criterion All demonstrator service-to-service communication is protected by the configured service mesh and untrusted paths are blocked. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-001/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given the service mesh is deployed in each target cluster with workload identities issued When two in-mesh services communicate and a workload outside the mesh attempts the same call Then the in-mesh call is carried over the mesh under mutual TLS AND the out-of-mesh call is blocked and logged. ZT-02 — Secure Execution Environment ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-002 Acceptance criterion Critical components run only in the protected Kubernetes execution environment with signed-image/admission controls active. Test type BDD / integration Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-002/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/admission.feature Given the target Kubernetes environment is ready and the approved signed release artefacts are available When the Zero Trust execution environment is deployed Then only artefacts satisfying the configured admission and trust controls reach Running state AND an unsigned or non-compliant artefact is rejected before execution. ZT-03 — Trust Zone ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-003 Acceptance criterion The two federation/trust zones are represented as separate participants with isolated cluster contexts and explicit trust relationships. Test type BDD / integration Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-003/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/trust-lists.feature Given the two federation zones are deployed as separate participants in isolated cluster contexts When the configured trust relationship between them is exercised Then each zone resolves the other as an explicitly configured participant AND a zone outside the configured relationship is not resolvable as a participant. ZT-04 — Secure Connection ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-004 Acceptance criterion ZT Connector A and ZT Connector B establish a protected authenticated channel before application traffic is permitted. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-004/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given two configured Zero Trust Connectors with trusted identities When Connector A initiates a connection to Connector B Then an authenticated protected channel is established before application traffic is forwarded AND a peer that cannot establish the required trusted channel receives no application traffic. ZT-05 — Communication Visualization ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-005 Acceptance criterion The demonstrator visibly presents connection/trust state, decisions and communication outcomes to an external audience. Test type UX/BDD Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-005/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/visualization.feature Given the client-approved visualization concept and a running FACIS.ZTD demonstrator When the communication-visualization scenario is exercised through the ORCE-orchestrated user journey Then the demonstrator visibly presents connection and trust state, the decisions taken and the resulting communication outcomes to an external audience AND a blocked communication is presented with its refusal reason. ZT-06 — Attribute/Credential Based Access Control ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-006 Acceptance criterion Participant-backend access to protected resources is decided from verified attributes/credentials and corresponding policy rules. Access control is applied as attribute-based access control (ABAC) on the inner channel from participant backend to protected resource. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-006/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/policy.feature Given one participant backend with the required credential attributes and one without them When both request the same protected resource Then the authorized request is permitted according to credential/policy evaluation AND the request without matching attributes/authorization is denied and evidenced. ZT-07 — API Dock ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-007 Acceptance criterion A participant-backend API and protected-resource API can be integrated/replaced through documented interfaces without changing the Zero Trust core. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-007/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/authorization.feature Given the documented participant-backend and protected-resource interfaces When a replacement API is docked in place of the supplied mock Then it serves the demonstrator flow with no change to Connector, policy or trust configuration AND an API that does not satisfy the documented interface is rejected at configuration time. ZT-08 — Visualization ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-008 Acceptance criterion The UI presents the key Zero Trust functionality and full demonstrator flow in a comprehensible client-approved visualization. Test type UX/BDD Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-008/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/visualization.feature Given the client-approved visualization concept and a running demonstrator When an external observer follows the demonstrator flow in the UI Then the key Zero Trust functionality and the complete flow are presented comprehensibly in the approved form AND a step that produces no visible outcome is recorded as a defect. ZT-09 — User Journey ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-009 Acceptance criterion The client-aligned scenario is orchestrated step by step by ORCE and demonstrates the complete end-to-end Zero Trust flow. Test type UX/BDD Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-009/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/visualization.feature Given the client-aligned user-journey scenario configured in ORCE When the journey is run from participant registration through to the protected-resource response Then ORCE orchestrates each step in sequence and the complete end-to-end Zero Trust flow is demonstrated AND a failing step halts the journey with its reason shown. ZT-10 — Image Signing and Attestation ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-010 Acceptance criterion Custom GitHub runner up and running, Key material can be uploaded on the runner, Runner setup AMD64-based systems. Signing and attestation flows can be triggered by authorised maintainers and committers only. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-010/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/supply-chain.feature Given the approved GitHub runner, signing key material and a release image When the image-signing and mock-attestation workflow runs Then the image is signed and the attestation artefact is produced by the authorized pipeline AND a release without the required signature cannot pass the admission path. ZT-11 — OPA Gatekeeper ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-011 Acceptance criterion All Docker images signed by the client, Gatekeeper blocks unsigned images during pod creation, Trust Anchor is provided via did:web, Other Governance Rego Policies can be executed over Gatekeeper, e.g., allowed registries, naming conventions or similar. Trust anchor key material is stored in OpenBao, or used via the transit engine and TSA crypto provider service, and is linked over TRAIN. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-011/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/admission.feature Given OPA Gatekeeper deployed with the client trust anchor published via did:web over TSA and linked in TRAIN, and the signing key material held in OpenBao When pods are created from a correctly signed image and from an unsigned image Then the signed image is admitted and the unsigned image is blocked at pod creation AND additional governance Rego policies, such as allowed registries and naming conventions, are enforced through Gatekeeper. ZT-12 — OPA Policy Repository ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-012 Acceptance criterion Policy artifacts can be built and uploaded to Harbor; Gatekeeper loads and uses the policies from Harbor. Policy packages are built from a repository path to which only authorised maintainers and committers have write access. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-012/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/admission.feature Given an approved Rego policy package in the FACIS source repository When the GitHub Actions policy workflow runs Then the policy artefact is built and pushed to Harbor via OCI and Gatekeeper loads the published policy AND an unavailable or invalid policy package is not treated as an approved admission policy. ZT-13 — Linux-based Docker Images ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-013 Acceptance criterion All Docker images are Linux-based, All Docker images up and running. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-013/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/supply-chain.feature Given the release image set for the demonstrator When the images are inspected and deployed to the target cluster Then every image is Linux-based and reaches Running state AND an image that is not Linux-based is rejected before deployment. ZT-14 — T-Systems Open Sovereign Cloud Environment ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-014 Acceptance criterion Cluster and the solution are reachable. All ZT components deployed and in Running state, OPA Gatekeeper demonstrably blocking unsigned images, End-to-end connection between ZT Connector and protected resource verified. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-014/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/environments.feature Given the T-Systems Open Sovereign Cloud environment provisioned for the demonstrator When the full Zero Trust stack is deployed to it Then the cluster and solution are reachable, all Zero Trust components reach Running state, OPA Gatekeeper demonstrably blocks an unsigned image, and an end-to-end connection between the ZT Connector and the protected resource is verified. ZT-15 — IONOS Cloud Environment ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-015 Acceptance criterion Visualization of the Demonstrator runs on the IONOS Cloud. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-015/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/environments.feature Given the IONOS Kubernetes environment and the approved visualization release When the visualization stack is deployed Then the FACIS Zero Trust Demonstrator visualization is reachable and operational on IONOS Cloud. ZT-16 — Cloud Environments ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-016 Acceptance criterion Documentation can be demonstrated for reproducing the setup of each test cluster step- by-step. Test type Documentation / client review Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-016/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/documentation.feature Given the accepted release baseline When cloud environments documentation is generated from the repository Then the documented setup/usage can be reproduced step by step and the documentation is buildable from GitHub. ZT-17 — Demonstrator Usage ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-017 Acceptance criterion Documentation can be demonstrated for reproducing the setup of each test cluster step-by-step. The Demonstrator manual is generated automatically by a GitHub Actions workflow and published. Test type Documentation / client review Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-017/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/documentation.feature Given the accepted release baseline When demonstrator usage documentation is generated from the repository Then the documented setup/usage can be reproduced step by step and the documentation is buildable from GitHub. ZT-18 — TRAIN Allow List ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-018 Acceptance criterion Connector reads TRAIN trust lists to allow counter-connector connections. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-018/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/trust-lists.feature Given a TRAIN trust list naming the permitted counter-connector When connections are attempted from a listed and from an unlisted counter-connector Then the listed peer is admitted on the basis of the retrieved trust list AND the unlisted peer is refused. ZT-19 — Upstream / Downstream Proxy Functionality ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-019 Acceptance criterion Connector uses and establishes the TLS channel. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-019/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given two Zero Trust Connectors with an established attested TLS channel When an upstream request including relevant HTTP/gRPC metadata is forwarded through the connector pair Then the request reaches the counter side over that protected channel with required call information preserved AND no unprotected inter-connector path is used. ZT-20 — Guarding Functionality ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-020 Acceptance criterion Connector can guard a protected resource, No access without matching policies and authorizations. Enforcement is based on Rego policies evaluated through the TSA Policy Engine; the guard is deployable per protected resource over both REST and gRPC; unauthorised access is answered with an OID4VP link. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-020/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/authorization.feature Given a protected resource behind the Connector guard When a request with matching authorization and a request without matching authorization are executed Then the authorized request passes the PEP/PDP policy chain AND the unauthorized request is denied before the protected resource returns data. ZT-21 — OAuth2 Server ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-021 Acceptance criterion Server issues access tokens based on OID4VP presentations, Server issues access tokens to participant backends for accessing the connector itself. New participant backends are registered through Dynamic Client Registration. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-021/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/authorization.feature Given a registered participant backend and a valid OID4VP presentation When the Connector OAuth2 server processes the respective flows Then it issues the appropriate DPoP-bound access tokens AND an invalid presentation or unregistered/unauthorized client does not receive a usable access token. ZT-22 — Token Storage ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-022 Acceptance criterion Participant backend can call the protected resource over the connector, Upstream authorization is replaced via the token storage on DPOP basis. The token store performs token renewal and the associated OID4VP tasks without manual intervention. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-022/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/authorization.feature Given a participant-backend token and a stored counter-connector resource token When the backend calls the protected resource through the Connector Then the backend token and DPoP proof are validated and the correct counter-side token is used upstream AND an invalid DPoP proof or expired/unrenewable token causes the request to be denied. ZT-23 — Service Mesh Implementation ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-023 Acceptance criterion A service mesh based on Istio or Cilium is implemented in each Kubernetes cluster, Communication between services is routed through the service mesh. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-023/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given each target Kubernetes cluster with the selected Istio- or Cilium-based service mesh installed When services communicate within a cluster Then the mesh is present in every cluster and service traffic is routed through it AND traffic attempting to bypass the mesh data path is not delivered. ZT-24 — SPIFFE/SPIRE Deployment ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-024 Acceptance criterion SPIRE is deployed in each Kubernetes cluster, The service mesh is configured to use SPIRE-provided identities, Appropriate SPIRE node- and workload attestation is used, All services participating in the service mesh are registered as SPIRE workloads. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-024/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/workload-identity.feature Given each target Kubernetes cluster is running When SPIRE node and workload registration is applied Then SPIRE is deployed in every cluster, all mesh services obtain SPIRE-backed identities and the service mesh uses those identities AND a workload that cannot attest does not receive an identity. ZT-25 — Routing Policies ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-025 Acceptance criterion The service mesh is configured to enforce network policies, Network policies are deployed to allow related services to communicate, A default deny policy is in place to prevent unaffiliated service communication. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-025/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given related and unrelated workloads in the service mesh When east-west communication is attempted Then policy-related workloads communicate according to configured trust policy AND unaffiliated workloads are blocked by the default-deny network policy without relying on IP-address identity. ZT-26 — Ingress and Egress ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-026 Acceptance criterion Ingress and egress for all inter-service communication is configured to use the ZT connector, Other APIs use a different appropriate ingress and egress configuration. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-026/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given application traffic, DNS traffic and an observability/admin endpoint When each traffic type leaves or enters a cluster Then protected inter-cluster application traffic is routed through the ZT Connector AND explicitly exempt infrastructure/admin traffic uses its separately controlled ingress/egress path. ZT-27 — Observability ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-027 Acceptance criterion OTEL logs available. Telemetry is exported through the OpenTelemetry Collector, metrics are retained in Prometheus and traces are available in an OTel-compatible tracing backend. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-027/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given the OpenTelemetry Collector, Prometheus and the OTel-compatible tracing backend are deployed When demonstrator traffic and security decisions occur Then traces and metrics are exported from the cluster through the Collector, metrics are retained in Prometheus and traces are queryable in the tracing backend AND a component emitting no telemetry is visible as a gap in the correlated trace. ZT-28 — Attested TLS ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-028 Acceptance criterion All inter-cluster communication uses the attested TLS protocol, An appropriate TLS version is used, TLS certificates are correctly checked against the cluster’s identities. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-028/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given two ZT Connectors in different clusters When they establish inter-cluster communication Then the channel uses mutually attested TLS with TLS 1.3 or later and certificates are checked against cluster identity AND a TLS version below 1.3 or failed identity/attestation validation prevents channel establishment. ZT-29 — Attestation Request ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-029 Acceptance criterion The attestation request message is sent in a machine-readable format, The information contained in the message includes the desired attestation type, including at least: • Server-Side Attestation: Only the server provides an attestation report, • Client-Side Attestation: Only the client provides an attestation report, • Mutual Attestation: Both server and client provide an attestation report. The size of any additional information contained in the message does not exceed the size of the attestation report. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-029/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given a Connector initiates an attested-TLS handshake When it creates an attestation request Then the request is machine-readable and states the requested server-side, client-side or mutual attestation mode AND malformed requests or unsupported required attestation information do not advance the handshake. ZT-30 — Attestation Response ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-030 Acceptance criterion The attestation response message is sent in a machine-readable format, The attestation response contains an attestation report, The size of any additional information contained in the message does not exceed the size of the attestation report. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-030/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given a valid machine-readable attestation request When the peer creates its response Then the response contains the required attestation report (or an empty/null report where none was requested) and respects the specified size constraint AND malformed responses are rejected by the receiving protocol flow. ZT-31 — Attestation Report Format ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-031 Acceptance criterion All attestation report signatures can be verified using common cryptography libraries (e.g. OpenSSL), All attestation reports can be verified by the receiver without special knowledge; if additional information besides the attestation report is needed (e.g. an intermediary certificate), it is provided in TRAIN or as part of the attestation response message, All attestation reports contain the TLS-exporter channel binding for the TLS channel through which they are sent. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-031/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given an attestation report received during the TLS handshake When the peer verifies it Then the report signature is cryptographically verifiable, required supporting information is available, and the TLS-exporter channel binding matches the active TLS channel AND a report with invalid signature or channel binding is rejected. ZT-32 — Verification Result Message ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-032 Acceptance criterion The verification result message is sent in a machine-readable format, An affirmative verification result message is sent only if the attestation report sent by the peer could be verified successfully, The size of any additional information contained in the message does not exceed the size of the attestation report. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-032/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given a peer has completed attestation-report verification When it sends the verification-result message Then the message is machine-readable and affirmative only after successful verification AND a failed verification never produces an affirmative result. ZT-33 — Error Message ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-033 Acceptance criterion For any error case in each peer implementation, an error message is sent, The error message is machine-readable, The size of any additional information contained in the message does not exceed the size of the attestation report, Error messages are correctly received and lead to connection termination. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-033/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given an error occurs at any defined step of the attestation protocol When the peer handles the error Then it emits a machine-readable error containing a useful human-readable diagnostic and closes the TLS connection AND no application-layer communication continues after the error. ZT-34 — Proxy Integration ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-034 Acceptance criterion The attested-TLS reverse proxy is configured from Kubernetes Ingress or Gateway API resources, integrates with the service mesh for inbound routing to member services, and is implemented in Go. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-034/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given an Ingress or Gateway API resource declaring an attested-TLS-protected route When the resource is applied and a peer connector initiates an attested connection Then the reverse proxy accepts the attested upstream connection and routes it to the configured in-mesh backend AND a route whose peer cannot be attested receives no application traffic. ZT-35 — Hash Management/TRAIN Integration ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-035 Acceptance criterion Upon connection establishment, the attested TLS endpoint fetches the peer’s hash from TRAIN, Connection establishment proceeds only if the hash matches the value in the attestation report. Each endpoint's CI/CD pipeline pre-generates its own launch digest and uploads it to TRAIN on every deployment. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-035/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/trust-lists.feature Given each attested-TLS endpoint has published its expected launch digest/measurement to TRAIN When a peer connection is established Then the remote expected hash is resolved from TRAIN and compared with the received attestation report AND a missing or mismatching trusted hash prevents connection establishment. ZT-36 — OPA Gatekeeper ¶ Test ID BDD-ZT-036 Acceptance criterion Gatekeeper consumes the policies and enforces them. Test type Lifecycle BDD (every release) Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-tdr-004/ Automation status implemented, runs on a cluster Evidence basis recorded per run Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/lifecycle.feature Test data features/fixtures/charts/lifecycle-fixture/ — the release under test (fixture); features/fixtures/charts/lifecycle-fixture/ci/values.yaml — its valid baseline values; INVALID in features/js/steps/lifecycle.steps.mjs — the invalid-parameter examples Given a deployed release When the uninstall workflow is executed Then the release is removed without manual intervention and the expected project resources are no longer present. TDR-BDD-05 — Keycloak / policy / token integration ¶ Test ID BDD-TDR-005 Acceptance criterion Required Keycloak, policy and token integrations are reachable and produce the expected allow/deny behaviour. Test type Integration BDD Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-tdr-005/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/authorization.feature Given the target Keycloak, policy and token services are reachable When a valid and an invalid access flow are executed Then the valid flow is authorized and the invalid flow is denied with traceable evidence. TDR-BDD-06 — Structured logging and ORCE errors ¶ Test ID BDD-TDR-006 Acceptance criterion Relevant runtime logs are structured JSON and automation errors are machine-readable and exposed through ORCE context. Test type Inspection / negative-path BDD Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-tdr-006/ Automation status implemented, runs on a cluster Evidence basis recorded per run Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/orce-qa.feature Test data features/fixtures/charts/lifecycle-fixture/ — the release the controlled error targets; the chart value rejected example of INVALID in features/js/steps/lifecycle.steps.mjs Given a controlled error condition When it is triggered Then the corresponding log is structured JSON and the machine-readable error is available through the ORCE context. TDR-BDD-07 — TLS 1.3 runtime validation ¶ Test ID BDD-TDR-007 Acceptance criterion TLS 1.3 is enforced on all relevant endpoints and older TLS protocol versions are rejected. Test type Security BDD Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-tdr-007/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/security-baseline.feature Given the deployed endpoints When TLS 1.3 and an older TLS version are attempted Then TLS 1.3 succeeds where authorized and the older protocol version is rejected. TDR-BDD-08 — Secrets and log masking ¶ Test ID BDD-TDR-008 Acceptance criterion Credentials/secrets are stored in Kubernetes Secrets and no plaintext secret is exposed in application or pipeline logs. Test type Security inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-tdr-008/ Automation status implemented, runs on a cluster Evidence basis recorded per run Runner godog Scenario file features/go/security-baseline.feature Given the deployed release and CI/CD logs When secret storage and log output are inspected Then required credentials are held in Kubernetes Secrets and no plaintext secret value is present in logs. TDR-BDD-09 — Required Kubernetes objects ¶ Test ID BDD-TDR-009 Acceptance criterion Namespace, ingress, service and deployment objects required for the release are created correctly. Test type Deployment inspection (every release) Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-tdr-009/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/release-quality.feature Given a successful release deployment When the Kubernetes resources are inspected Then the required namespace, ingress, service and deployment objects exist and are ready. TDR-BDD-10 — External dependency reachability ¶ Test ID BDD-TDR-010 Acceptance criterion Required external dependencies, including Keycloak and trust endpoints, are reachable from the prescribed target environment. Test type Integration readiness test Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-tdr-010/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/environments.feature Given the target deployment When dependency health/connectivity checks are executed Then the required Keycloak and trust endpoints are reachable and their expected interfaces respond. TDR-BDD-11 — Helm lint and dry-run ¶ Test ID BDD-TDR-011 Acceptance criterion Every release Helm chart passes lint and dry-run checks before promotion. Test type CI quality gate (every release) Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-tdr-011/ Automation status implemented, runs on a cluster Evidence basis recorded per run Runner godog Scenario file features/go/release-quality.feature Given a release candidate When its Helm chart enters the CI quality gate Then helm lint and helm dry-run both pass before the release can be promoted. M7-01 — Final Validation and Demonstration ¶ Test ID BDD-M7-001 Acceptance criterion The complete demonstrator is validated with the client in the agreed target environment. The approved user journey, the positive path and the refusal paths are demonstrated end to end, every demonstrated state is traceable to the per-gate evidence bundle, and no open Critical/High release blocker exists at the time of the demonstration. Test type Acceptance demonstration / client review Gate G7 - Final validation Evidence evidence/bdd-m7-001/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/final-acceptance.feature Given the release accepted at G6 and the agreed target environment When the final validation session is executed with FACIS Then the complete approved user journey, the positive path and the refusal paths are demonstrated end to end AND every demonstrated state is traceable to the per-gate evidence bundle AND no open Critical/High release blocker is present. M7-02 — Joint Final Report ¶ Test ID BDD-M7-002 Acceptance criterion The joint final report is prepared together with the client and contains resolvable references to the SRS, the Technical Development Requirements, the approved project plan, the agreed acceptance criteria and the per-gate evidence bundle. Test type Documentation / client review Gate G7 - Final validation Evidence evidence/bdd-m7-002/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/final-acceptance.feature Given the completed per-gate evidence bundles and the accepted release When the joint final report is prepared and reviewed with FACIS Then the report is complete and every one of its five required references resolves to the referenced artefact AND the client records its acceptance of the report.
