docs.title: BDD catalogue

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-001 Acceptance criterion All demonstrator service-to-service communication is protected by the configured service mesh and untrusted paths are blocked. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-001/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given the service mesh is deployed in each target cluster with workload identities issued When two in-mesh services communicate and a workload outside the mesh attempts the same call Then the in-mesh call is carried over the mesh under mutual TLS AND the out-of-mesh call is blocked and logged.
docs.title: ZT-01 — Secure Service Mesh

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-002 Acceptance criterion Critical components run only in the protected Kubernetes execution environment with signed-image/admission controls active. Test type BDD / integration Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-002/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/admission.feature Given the target Kubernetes environment is ready and the approved signed release artefacts are available When the Zero Trust execution environment is deployed Then only artefacts satisfying the configured admission and trust controls reach Running state AND an unsigned or non-compliant artefact is rejected before execution.
docs.title: ZT-02 — Secure Execution Environment

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-003 Acceptance criterion The two federation/trust zones are represented as separate participants with isolated cluster contexts and explicit trust relationships. Test type BDD / integration Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-003/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/trust-lists.feature Given the two federation zones are deployed as separate participants in isolated cluster contexts When the configured trust relationship between them is exercised Then each zone resolves the other as an explicitly configured participant AND a zone outside the configured relationship is not resolvable as a participant.
docs.title: ZT-03 — Trust Zone

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-004 Acceptance criterion ZT Connector A and ZT Connector B establish a protected authenticated channel before application traffic is permitted. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-004/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given two configured Zero Trust Connectors with trusted identities When Connector A initiates a connection to Connector B Then an authenticated protected channel is established before application traffic is forwarded AND a peer that cannot establish the required trusted channel receives no application traffic.
docs.title: ZT-04 — Secure Connection

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-005 Acceptance criterion The demonstrator visibly presents connection/trust state, decisions and communication outcomes to an external audience. Test type UX/BDD Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-005/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/visualization.feature Given the client-approved visualization concept and a running FACIS.ZTD demonstrator When the communication-visualization scenario is exercised through the ORCE-orchestrated user journey Then the demonstrator visibly presents connection and trust state, the decisions taken and the resulting communication outcomes to an external audience AND a blocked communication is presented with its refusal reason.
docs.title: ZT-05 — Communication Visualization

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-006 Acceptance criterion Participant-backend access to protected resources is decided from verified attributes/credentials and corresponding policy rules. Access control is applied as attribute-based access control (ABAC) on the inner channel from participant backend to protected resource. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-006/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/policy.feature Given one participant backend with the required credential attributes and one without them When both request the same protected resource Then the authorized request is permitted according to credential/policy evaluation AND the request without matching attributes/authorization is denied and evidenced.
docs.title: ZT-06 — Attribute/Credential Based Access Control

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-007 Acceptance criterion A participant-backend API and protected-resource API can be integrated/replaced through documented interfaces without changing the Zero Trust core. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-007/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/authorization.feature Given the documented participant-backend and protected-resource interfaces When a replacement API is docked in place of the supplied mock Then it serves the demonstrator flow with no change to Connector, policy or trust configuration AND an API that does not satisfy the documented interface is rejected at configuration time.
docs.title: ZT-07 — API Dock

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-008 Acceptance criterion The UI presents the key Zero Trust functionality and full demonstrator flow in a comprehensible client-approved visualization. Test type UX/BDD Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-008/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/visualization.feature Given the client-approved visualization concept and a running demonstrator When an external observer follows the demonstrator flow in the UI Then the key Zero Trust functionality and the complete flow are presented comprehensibly in the approved form AND a step that produces no visible outcome is recorded as a defect.
docs.title: ZT-08 — Visualization

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-009 Acceptance criterion The client-aligned scenario is orchestrated step by step by ORCE and demonstrates the complete end-to-end Zero Trust flow. Test type UX/BDD Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-009/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/visualization.feature Given the client-aligned user-journey scenario configured in ORCE When the journey is run from participant registration through to the protected-resource response Then ORCE orchestrates each step in sequence and the complete end-to-end Zero Trust flow is demonstrated AND a failing step halts the journey with its reason shown.
docs.title: ZT-09 — User Journey

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-010 Acceptance criterion Custom GitHub runner up and running, Key material can be uploaded on the runner, Runner setup AMD64-based systems. Signing and attestation flows can be triggered by authorised maintainers and committers only. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-010/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/supply-chain.feature Given the approved GitHub runner, signing key material and a release image When the image-signing and mock-attestation workflow runs Then the image is signed and the attestation artefact is produced by the authorized pipeline AND a release without the required signature cannot pass the admission path.
docs.title: ZT-10 — Image Signing and Attestation

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-011 Acceptance criterion All Docker images signed by the client, Gatekeeper blocks unsigned images during pod creation, Trust Anchor is provided via did:web, Other Governance Rego Policies can be executed over Gatekeeper, e.g., allowed registries, naming conventions or similar. Trust anchor key material is stored in OpenBao, or used via the transit engine and TSA crypto provider service, and is linked over TRAIN. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-011/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/admission.feature Given OPA Gatekeeper deployed with the client trust anchor published via did:web over TSA and linked in TRAIN, and the signing key material held in OpenBao When pods are created from a correctly signed image and from an unsigned image Then the signed image is admitted and the unsigned image is blocked at pod creation AND additional governance Rego policies, such as allowed registries and naming conventions, are enforced through Gatekeeper.
docs.title: ZT-11 — OPA Gatekeeper

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-012 Acceptance criterion Policy artifacts can be built and uploaded to Harbor; Gatekeeper loads and uses the policies from Harbor. Policy packages are built from a repository path to which only authorised maintainers and committers have write access. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-012/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/admission.feature Given an approved Rego policy package in the FACIS source repository When the GitHub Actions policy workflow runs Then the policy artefact is built and pushed to Harbor via OCI and Gatekeeper loads the published policy AND an unavailable or invalid policy package is not treated as an approved admission policy.
docs.title: ZT-12 — OPA Policy Repository

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-013 Acceptance criterion All Docker images are Linux-based, All Docker images up and running. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-013/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/supply-chain.feature Given the release image set for the demonstrator When the images are inspected and deployed to the target cluster Then every image is Linux-based and reaches Running state AND an image that is not Linux-based is rejected before deployment.
docs.title: ZT-13 — Linux-based Docker Images

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-014 Acceptance criterion Cluster and the solution are reachable. All ZT components deployed and in Running state, OPA Gatekeeper demonstrably blocking unsigned images, End-to-end connection between ZT Connector and protected resource verified. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-014/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/environments.feature Given the T-Systems Open Sovereign Cloud environment provisioned for the demonstrator When the full Zero Trust stack is deployed to it Then the cluster and solution are reachable, all Zero Trust components reach Running state, OPA Gatekeeper demonstrably blocks an unsigned image, and an end-to-end connection between the ZT Connector and the protected resource is verified.
docs.title: ZT-14 — T-Systems Open Sovereign Cloud Environment

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-015 Acceptance criterion Visualization of the Demonstrator runs on the IONOS Cloud. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-015/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/environments.feature Given the IONOS Kubernetes environment and the approved visualization release When the visualization stack is deployed Then the FACIS Zero Trust Demonstrator visualization is reachable and operational on IONOS Cloud.
docs.title: ZT-15 — IONOS Cloud Environment

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-016 Acceptance criterion Documentation can be demonstrated for reproducing the setup of each test cluster step- by-step. Test type Documentation / client review Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-016/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/documentation.feature Given the accepted release baseline When cloud environments documentation is generated from the repository Then the documented setup/usage can be reproduced step by step and the documentation is buildable from GitHub.
docs.title: ZT-16 — Cloud Environments

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-017 Acceptance criterion Documentation can be demonstrated for reproducing the setup of each test cluster step-by-step. The Demonstrator manual is generated automatically by a GitHub Actions workflow and published. Test type Documentation / client review Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-017/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/documentation.feature Given the accepted release baseline When demonstrator usage documentation is generated from the repository Then the documented setup/usage can be reproduced step by step and the documentation is buildable from GitHub.
docs.title: ZT-17 — Demonstrator Usage

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-018 Acceptance criterion Connector reads TRAIN trust lists to allow counter-connector connections. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-018/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/trust-lists.feature Given a TRAIN trust list naming the permitted counter-connector When connections are attempted from a listed and from an unlisted counter-connector Then the listed peer is admitted on the basis of the retrieved trust list AND the unlisted peer is refused.
docs.title: ZT-18 — TRAIN Allow List

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-019 Acceptance criterion Connector uses and establishes the TLS channel. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-019/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given two Zero Trust Connectors with an established attested TLS channel When an upstream request including relevant HTTP/gRPC metadata is forwarded through the connector pair Then the request reaches the counter side over that protected channel with required call information preserved AND no unprotected inter-connector path is used.
docs.title: ZT-19 — Upstream / Downstream Proxy Functionality

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-020 Acceptance criterion Connector can guard a protected resource, No access without matching policies and authorizations. Enforcement is based on Rego policies evaluated through the TSA Policy Engine; the guard is deployable per protected resource over both REST and gRPC; unauthorised access is answered with an OID4VP link. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-020/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/authorization.feature Given a protected resource behind the Connector guard When a request with matching authorization and a request without matching authorization are executed Then the authorized request passes the PEP/PDP policy chain AND the unauthorized request is denied before the protected resource returns data.
docs.title: ZT-20 — Guarding Functionality

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-021 Acceptance criterion Server issues access tokens based on OID4VP presentations, Server issues access tokens to participant backends for accessing the connector itself. New participant backends are registered through Dynamic Client Registration. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-021/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/authorization.feature Given a registered participant backend and a valid OID4VP presentation When the Connector OAuth2 server processes the respective flows Then it issues the appropriate DPoP-bound access tokens AND an invalid presentation or unregistered/unauthorized client does not receive a usable access token.
docs.title: ZT-21 — OAuth2 Server

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-022 Acceptance criterion Participant backend can call the protected resource over the connector, Upstream authorization is replaced via the token storage on DPOP basis. The token store performs token renewal and the associated OID4VP tasks without manual intervention. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-022/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/authorization.feature Given a participant-backend token and a stored counter-connector resource token When the backend calls the protected resource through the Connector Then the backend token and DPoP proof are validated and the correct counter-side token is used upstream AND an invalid DPoP proof or expired/unrenewable token causes the request to be denied.
docs.title: ZT-22 — Token Storage

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-023 Acceptance criterion A service mesh based on Istio or Cilium is implemented in each Kubernetes cluster, Communication between services is routed through the service mesh. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-023/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given each target Kubernetes cluster with the selected Istio- or Cilium-based service mesh installed When services communicate within a cluster Then the mesh is present in every cluster and service traffic is routed through it AND traffic attempting to bypass the mesh data path is not delivered.
docs.title: ZT-23 — Service Mesh Implementation

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-024 Acceptance criterion SPIRE is deployed in each Kubernetes cluster, The service mesh is configured to use SPIRE-provided identities, Appropriate SPIRE node- and workload attestation is used, All services participating in the service mesh are registered as SPIRE workloads. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-024/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/workload-identity.feature Given each target Kubernetes cluster is running When SPIRE node and workload registration is applied Then SPIRE is deployed in every cluster, all mesh services obtain SPIRE-backed identities and the service mesh uses those identities AND a workload that cannot attest does not receive an identity.
docs.title: ZT-24 — SPIFFE/SPIRE Deployment

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-025 Acceptance criterion The service mesh is configured to enforce network policies, Network policies are deployed to allow related services to communicate, A default deny policy is in place to prevent unaffiliated service communication. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-025/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given related and unrelated workloads in the service mesh When east-west communication is attempted Then policy-related workloads communicate according to configured trust policy AND unaffiliated workloads are blocked by the default-deny network policy without relying on IP-address identity.
docs.title: ZT-25 — Routing Policies

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-026 Acceptance criterion Ingress and egress for all inter-service communication is configured to use the ZT connector, Other APIs use a different appropriate ingress and egress configuration. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-026/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given application traffic, DNS traffic and an observability/admin endpoint When each traffic type leaves or enters a cluster Then protected inter-cluster application traffic is routed through the ZT Connector AND explicitly exempt infrastructure/admin traffic uses its separately controlled ingress/egress path.
docs.title: ZT-26 — Ingress and Egress

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-027 Acceptance criterion OTEL logs available. Telemetry is exported through the OpenTelemetry Collector, metrics are retained in Prometheus and traces are available in an OTel-compatible tracing backend. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-027/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given the OpenTelemetry Collector, Prometheus and the OTel-compatible tracing backend are deployed When demonstrator traffic and security decisions occur Then traces and metrics are exported from the cluster through the Collector, metrics are retained in Prometheus and traces are queryable in the tracing backend AND a component emitting no telemetry is visible as a gap in the correlated trace.
docs.title: ZT-27 — Observability

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-028 Acceptance criterion All inter-cluster communication uses the attested TLS protocol, An appropriate TLS version is used, TLS certificates are correctly checked against the cluster’s identities. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-028/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given two ZT Connectors in different clusters When they establish inter-cluster communication Then the channel uses mutually attested TLS with TLS 1.3 or later and certificates are checked against cluster identity AND a TLS version below 1.3 or failed identity/attestation validation prevents channel establishment.
docs.title: ZT-28 — Attested TLS

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-029 Acceptance criterion The attestation request message is sent in a machine-readable format, The information contained in the message includes the desired attestation type, including at least: • Server-Side Attestation: Only the server provides an attestation report, • Client-Side Attestation: Only the client provides an attestation report, • Mutual Attestation: Both server and client provide an attestation report. The size of any additional information contained in the message does not exceed the size of the attestation report. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-029/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given a Connector initiates an attested-TLS handshake When it creates an attestation request Then the request is machine-readable and states the requested server-side, client-side or mutual attestation mode AND malformed requests or unsupported required attestation information do not advance the handshake.
docs.title: ZT-29 — Attestation Request

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-030 Acceptance criterion The attestation response message is sent in a machine-readable format, The attestation response contains an attestation report, The size of any additional information contained in the message does not exceed the size of the attestation report. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-030/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given a valid machine-readable attestation request When the peer creates its response Then the response contains the required attestation report (or an empty/null report where none was requested) and respects the specified size constraint AND malformed responses are rejected by the receiving protocol flow.
docs.title: ZT-30 — Attestation Response

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-031 Acceptance criterion All attestation report signatures can be verified using common cryptography libraries (e.g. OpenSSL), All attestation reports can be verified by the receiver without special knowledge; if additional information besides the attestation report is needed (e.g. an intermediary certificate), it is provided in TRAIN or as part of the attestation response message, All attestation reports contain the TLS-exporter channel binding for the TLS channel through which they are sent. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-031/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given an attestation report received during the TLS handshake When the peer verifies it Then the report signature is cryptographically verifiable, required supporting information is available, and the TLS-exporter channel binding matches the active TLS channel AND a report with invalid signature or channel binding is rejected.
docs.title: ZT-31 — Attestation Report Format

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-032 Acceptance criterion The verification result message is sent in a machine-readable format, An affirmative verification result message is sent only if the attestation report sent by the peer could be verified successfully, The size of any additional information contained in the message does not exceed the size of the attestation report. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-032/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given a peer has completed attestation-report verification When it sends the verification-result message Then the message is machine-readable and affirmative only after successful verification AND a failed verification never produces an affirmative result.
docs.title: ZT-32 — Verification Result Message

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-033 Acceptance criterion For any error case in each peer implementation, an error message is sent, The error message is machine-readable, The size of any additional information contained in the message does not exceed the size of the attestation report, Error messages are correctly received and lead to connection termination. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-033/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given an error occurs at any defined step of the attestation protocol When the peer handles the error Then it emits a machine-readable error containing a useful human-readable diagnostic and closes the TLS connection AND no application-layer communication continues after the error.
docs.title: ZT-33 — Error Message

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-034 Acceptance criterion The attested-TLS reverse proxy is configured from Kubernetes Ingress or Gateway API resources, integrates with the service mesh for inbound routing to member services, and is implemented in Go. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-034/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given an Ingress or Gateway API resource declaring an attested-TLS-protected route When the resource is applied and a peer connector initiates an attested connection Then the reverse proxy accepts the attested upstream connection and routes it to the configured in-mesh backend AND a route whose peer cannot be attested receives no application traffic.
docs.title: ZT-34 — Proxy Integration

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-035 Acceptance criterion Upon connection establishment, the attested TLS endpoint fetches the peer’s hash from TRAIN, Connection establishment proceeds only if the hash matches the value in the attestation report. Each endpoint's CI/CD pipeline pre-generates its own launch digest and uploads it to TRAIN on every deployment. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-035/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/trust-lists.feature Given each attested-TLS endpoint has published its expected launch digest/measurement to TRAIN When a peer connection is established Then the remote expected hash is resolved from TRAIN and compared with the received attestation report AND a missing or mismatching trusted hash prevents connection establishment.
docs.title: ZT-35 — Hash Management/TRAIN Integration

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-036 Acceptance criterion Gatekeeper consumes the policies and enforces them. Gatekeeper loads Rego policy packages in combination with the XFSC TSA Policy Service. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-036/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/admission.feature Given OPA Gatekeeper deployed together with the XFSC TSA Policy Service and a published Rego policy package When a workload subject to that policy is submitted for admission Then Gatekeeper loads the policy through the TSA Policy Service and enforces the decision AND a workload violating the policy is denied at admission.
docs.title: ZT-36 — OPA Gatekeeper

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-037 Acceptance criterion Policies are available; a GitHub push action is in place. Policies are distributed as tarball packages through XFSC Harbor over the OCI interface. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-037/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/admission.feature Given an approved Gatekeeper/Rego policy source in the FACIS repository When the policy publication workflow runs Then the policy package is built and published to Harbor and the required GitHub push action completes successfully.
docs.title: ZT-37 — OPA Gatekeeper Policies

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-038 Acceptance criterion OPA Gatekeeper accepts Docker images which are signed by the client. The public verification keys are published so that signatures can be verified independently. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-038/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/supply-chain.feature Given a release image and the client-controlled signing setup When the GitHub Actions signing workflow completes Then the image signature is published and Gatekeeper accepts the correctly signed image AND an unsigned or incorrectly signed image is rejected at admission.
docs.title: ZT-38 — Container Signing Pipeline

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-039 Acceptance criterion Participant backend can register itself, Participant backend can obtain access tokens, Participant backend can successfully pass PEP proxy to connect Zero Trust connector and its channel, Participant backend gets an answer from protected resource mock, Visualization reflects this interaction. Test type BDD / integration Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-039/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/authorization.feature Given the participant-backend mock is configured against the ZT Connector When it dynamically registers and requests protected-resource access Then it obtains the required access token, passes the Connector/PEP path, receives the protected-resource response and exposes the interaction to the visualization AND a failed registration/authorization is surfaced as a refusal outcome.
docs.title: ZT-39 — Participant Backend Mockup

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-040 Acceptance criterion A participant backend can use the Zero Trust Channel of the Connector to call protected resource, and the Connector will add the obtained Access Tokens of the counter connector to each call, DPOP Verification of each participant backend call and matching it against internal JWT storage, OCM W-Stack Presentations can be triggered by using OID4VP Verifier requests from counter connector. Test type BDD / integration Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-040/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/credential-lifecycle.feature Given a participant backend with a valid credential presentation and DPoP-capable client identity When it accesses the counter-side protected resource through the ZT Connector Then the Connector obtains/maintains the counter-side access token via OCM/OID4VP, validates DPoP, substitutes the correct upstream authorization and returns the protected response AND revoked/invalid credentials, invalid DPoP or unusable tokens result in denial.
docs.title: ZT-40 — Credential-Based Access Control (CrBAC)

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-041 Acceptance criterion Protected resource responds different results based on roles. Test type BDD / integration Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-041/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/policy.feature Given the protected-resource mock configured with role-differentiated responses When it is called with access tokens carrying different roles Then each role receives its configured response AND a token carrying no permitted role receives no protected content.
docs.title: ZT-41 — Protected Resource Mockup

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-042 Acceptance criterion GitHub documentation and GitHub Page ready, Concept aligned with the client. Test type Documentation / client review Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/shared/bdd-zt-042-079/ — one shared execution for BDD-ZT-042 and BDD-ZT-079 Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/documentation.feature Given the initial demonstrator flow When the wireframe/visualization concept is reviewed with FACIS Then the concept is documented in GitHub and the client approval record is captured before UI implementation proceeds.
docs.title: ZT-42 — UX Concept

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-043 Acceptance criterion ORCE is used. Test type UX/BDD Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-043/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/visualization.feature Given the demonstrator deployed with ORCE as the orchestration runtime When the visualization user journey is executed Then every step of the journey is driven by an ORCE flow that is identifiable in the ORCE runtime AND no journey step bypasses ORCE.
docs.title: ZT-43 — ORCE Usage

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-044 Acceptance criterion Concept for value visualization aligned with the client, Values presented in Demonstrator. The presented values include TEE measurements, credentials, TRAIN zones, communication decisions and messages. Test type UX/BDD Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-044/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/visualization.feature Given the client-aligned value-visualization concept and a running demonstrator When the user journey produces trust and communication outcomes Then the demonstrator presents the TEE measurements, credentials, TRAIN zones, communication decisions and messages defined in the concept AND a value that cannot be obtained is shown as unavailable rather than omitted.
docs.title: ZT-44 — Value Visualization

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-045 Acceptance criterion Configuration documented, Configuration within the Demonstrator for certain parts can be demonstrated. The configuration interface covers TRAIN zones and policies. Test type UX/BDD Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-045/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/visualization.feature Given the documented demonstrator configuration interface When an operator changes the TRAIN zone and policy configuration through it Then the change is applied and reflected in the running demonstrator AND an invalid configuration is rejected with a machine-readable error.
docs.title: ZT-45 — Demonstrator Configuration

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-046 Acceptance criterion Scenario is aligned and documented on GitHub, Scenario is integrated into the Demonstrator and orchestrated by ORCE step-by- step, Scenario is illustrated with animations and images. The issuing process provides the credential to OCM W-Stack. Test type UX/BDD Gate G5 - Code ready for QA + ORCE user journey and visualization Evidence evidence/shared/bdd-zt-046-081/ — one shared execution for BDD-ZT-046 and BDD-ZT-081 Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner Cucumber.js Scenario file features/js/visualization.feature Given the client-approved user journey When it is executed in ORCE Then the journey is shown step by step, including credential issuance/presentation, trust decisions, protected-resource access and visual outcomes.
docs.title: ZT-46 — User Journey Scenario

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-047 Acceptance criterion All access requests require authentication and authorization, Session re-validation occurs at configurable intervals (≤ 15 minutes), Access is revoked automatically if session becomes non-compliant. Test type Negative-path BDD Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-047/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/fail-secure.feature Given an authenticated session with a configurable re-validation interval of 15 minutes or less When protected-resource requests continue over time Then authentication and authorization are re-evaluated at the configured interval AND access is revoked automatically when the session becomes non-compliant.
docs.title: ZT-47 — Continuous Authentication Enforcement

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-048 Acceptance criterion RBAC or ABAC is implemented, Privileged access rights are time-bound and require explicit approval, Test type BDD / integration Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-048/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/authorization.feature Given identities with different approved roles/attributes When they request functions with different privilege requirements Then each receives only the minimum permitted access and any privileged entitlement is time-bound/explicitly approved AND requests beyond the granted privilege are denied.
docs.title: ZT-48 — Least Privilege Access Control

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-049 Acceptance criterion Workloads are segmented by policy-defined trust zones, East-west traffic is inspected and authorized, Unauthorized lateral communication attempts are blocked and logged. Test type Negative-path BDD Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-049/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/plane-separation.feature Given workloads in separate policy-defined trust zones When authorized and unauthorized east-west connections are attempted Then permitted zone-to-zone traffic is inspected and authorized AND unauthorized lateral movement is blocked and logged.
docs.title: ZT-49 — Micro-Segmentation

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-050 Acceptance criterion No deprecated algorithms present in any component. Key lengths documented and auditable. Symmetric encryption uses AES-256 or equivalent, asymmetric encryption uses RSA-4096 or ECC P-256/P-384, and hash functions use SHA-256 or stronger. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-050/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/security-baseline.feature Given the deployed demonstrator configuration and generated cryptographic artefacts When algorithms, key lengths, hashes and TLS settings are inspected Then only BSI TR-02102-compliant algorithms/strengths are present and auditable AND deprecated algorithms such as MD5, SHA-1 or insufficient RSA key lengths are absent/rejected.
docs.title: ZT-50 — Cryptographic Standards (BSI TR-02102)

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-051 Acceptance criterion Revocation check performed at every credential verification. Revocation endpoint availability is monitored. Revocation uses a standards-compliant mechanism, either W3C Bitstring Status List v1.0 or IETF Token Status List, and unavailability of the revocation infrastructure results in fail-closed behaviour. Test type Negative-path BDD Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-051/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/credential-lifecycle.feature Given a credential is revoked or revocation status cannot be verified When the credential is presented for protected access Then verification fails closed and the protected resource is not reached.
docs.title: ZT-51 — Credential Revocation

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-052 Acceptance criterion Access denied when Policy Engine is unreachable (verified in test). Control plane failure detected and alerted within 30 seconds. Degradation scenarios documented with defined fail-closed behavior. Unavailability is demonstrated for each named control-plane component: Policy Engine, TRAIN, SPIRE and OCM. Test type Negative-path BDD Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-052/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/fail-secure.feature Given a required Zero Trust control-plane service becomes unavailable When protected access is requested Then access is denied, the failure is detected within 30 seconds and an alert/evidence record is produced.
docs.title: ZT-52 — Fail-Secure (Fail-Closed) Behavior

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-053 Acceptance criterion Tenant data, credentials and policy configuration are isolated by Kubernetes namespace; cross-tenant access attempts are denied and evidenced. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-053/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/plane-separation.feature Given two organizational tenants represented by separate Kubernetes namespaces When each tenant accesses its own and the other tenant's data, credentials or policy configuration Then own-tenant access follows authorization policy AND cross-tenant access is denied and evidenced.
docs.title: ZT-53 — Multi-Tenancy and Tenant Isolation

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-054 Acceptance criterion SBOM generated in CycloneDX or SPDX format for every release. SBOM published in GitHub repository alongside release artefacts. The SBOM is signed with the client's key material. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-054/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/supply-chain.feature Given a release build in the CI/CD pipeline When the release workflow completes Then an SBOM in CycloneDX or SPDX format is generated automatically, signed with the client key material and published in the repository alongside the release artefacts AND a release without a signed SBOM does not pass the release gate.
docs.title: ZT-54 — Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-055 Acceptance criterion Management plane components not reachable from data plane (verified in network test). Separation enforced at both network policy and service mesh layers. Architecture diagram clearly shows plane separation. The management-plane components covered are the Policy Engine, TRAIN, the SPIRE control plane, OCM and the observability stack. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-055/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/plane-separation.feature Given management-plane services and application/data-plane workloads are deployed When reachability is tested from both planes Then management services are reachable only through dedicated control channels and are separated by network-policy and service-mesh controls AND data-plane compromise/reachability does not provide access to management-plane endpoints.
docs.title: ZT-55 — Management Plane / Data Plane Separation

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-056 Acceptance criterion All third-party GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs. Pipeline runs with minimum REQUIRED permissions (no wildcard write access). No secrets visible in any pipeline log output. Pipeline-generated artefacts are signed before use, all pipeline runs are logged, and branch protection enforces code review before merge to main. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G6 - Quality readiness Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-056/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/supply-chain.feature Given the project GitHub Actions workflows and branch-protection configuration When a pipeline run and a merge to main are attempted Then all third-party actions are pinned to commit SHAs, the run holds only the minimum required permissions, no secret value appears in any log, artefacts are signed before use and the run is logged AND a merge to main without the required review is refused.
docs.title: ZT-56 — CI/CD Pipeline Security (Zero Trust for the Pipeline)

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-057 Acceptance criterion SPIFFE/SPIRE is set up and each microservice has access to a SPIRE Agent on the same node. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-057/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/workload-identity.feature Given the target Kubernetes nodes are ready When SPIFFE/SPIRE is installed and workloads are registered Then each relevant microservice has access to a SPIRE Agent on its node and can request workload identity.
docs.title: ZT-57 — SPIFFE/SPIRE Setup

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-058 Acceptance criterion The service mesh and control plane are enabled; traffic capture uses workload certificates for mutual TLS on each node. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-058/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given SPIRE-backed identities and the target clusters When the service mesh/control plane and traffic-capture layer are enabled Then service traffic is captured on each node and protected with workload-certificate-based mutual TLS.
docs.title: ZT-58 — Service Mesh Setup

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-059 Acceptance criterion The microservice successfully attests itself against the SPIRE Agent and receives an identity. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-059/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/workload-identity.feature Given a correctly registered microservice satisfying SPIRE attestation When it requests its workload identity Then SPIRE attests the workload successfully and issues the expected identity, which is then usable by the mesh.
docs.title: ZT-59 — Successful Identification

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-060 Acceptance criterion A microservice that fails SPIRE attestation receives no identity and cannot connect to any other service in the mesh. Test type Negative-path BDD Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-060/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/workload-identity.feature Given a workload cannot satisfy SPIRE attestation When it requests a workload identity and attempts mesh communication Then no identity is issued and all service communication is denied.
docs.title: ZT-60 — Unsuccessful Identification

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-061 Acceptance criterion All communication of the microservice is routed via the service mesh. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-061/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given a microservice participating in the configured mesh When it communicates with another service Then its service communication traverses the service-mesh data path and is subject to the configured identity and policy controls.
docs.title: ZT-61 — Traffic routed via Service Mesh

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-062 Acceptance criterion The microservice is only able to communicate with identities permitted in the configuration. Test type BDD / integration Gate G3 - Protected-service vertical slice Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-062/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/mesh.feature Given one identity explicitly permitted to communicate with a target service and one identity not permitted When both attempt the connection Then the permitted identity communicates successfully AND the non-permitted identity is blocked by mesh policy.
docs.title: ZT-62 — Limited Communication within Mesh

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-063 Acceptance criterion The TEE mock setup is enabled and generates demo attestations. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-063/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given the demonstrator remote-attestation environment When the TEE mock is started Then it produces the defined mock measurement/attestation material in the format required by the attested-TLS flow AND malformed/unavailable mock attestation material is not accepted as trusted evidence.
docs.title: ZT-63 — TEE Mock Setup

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-064 Acceptance criterion A ZT Connector can fetch expected mocked TEEM values from other connectors via TRAIN. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-064/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/trust-lists.feature Given a counter-connector has published its expected mocked TEE measurement to TRAIN When the Connector prepares to verify that peer Then it retrieves the expected measurement from TRAIN and uses it for comparison AND a peer with no published measurement cannot be verified.
docs.title: ZT-64 — Expected Measurement Retrieval

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-065 Acceptance criterion ZT Connector 1 starts a connection by sending an attestation request. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-065/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given Connector 1 is configured to establish an attested connection to Connector 2 When the connection starts Then Connector 1 sends the required machine-readable attestation request and the handshake enters the attestation flow.
docs.title: ZT-65 — Connection Start

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-066 Acceptance criterion ZT Connector 2 responds to the attestation request by creating an attestation report and sending it to ZT Connector 1. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-066/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given Connector 2 receives a valid attestation request When it performs remote attestation Then it creates the required attestation report and sends it to Connector 1 in the protocol response.
docs.title: ZT-66 — Remote Attestation

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-067 Acceptance criterion ZT Connector 1 verifies the attestation report by comparing the expected mocked TEEM against the mocked TEEM values in the TCR. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-067/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given Connector 1 has received Connector 2's attestation report and the expected mocked TEE measurement from the TCR/TRAIN path When verification is executed Then the observed and expected values plus cryptographic/channel-binding checks are validated AND any mismatch causes verification failure.
docs.title: ZT-67 — Attestation Report Verification

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-068 Acceptance criterion ZT Connector 1 informs ZT Connector 2 about the result of the verification. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-068/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given Connector 1 has completed verification of Connector 2's attestation report When it issues the verification-result message Then Connector 2 receives a machine-readable result reflecting the actual outcome AND a failed verification is reported as failure, never as success.
docs.title: ZT-68 — Verification Result

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-069 Acceptance criterion The handshake is successful and application-layer communication can take place via the established connection. Test type BDD / integration Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-069/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given a successful attested-TLS handshake between two Connectors When application traffic is sent over the established channel Then the traffic is carried end to end over that channel AND traffic offered before the handshake completes is not carried.
docs.title: ZT-69 — Established Connection

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-070 Acceptance criterion If handshake or attestation verification fails, no application-layer communication can take place. It is proven that no application-layer communication can take place. Test type Negative-path BDD Gate G4 - Bidirectional inter-cluster trust Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-070/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/attested-channel.feature Given the peer attestation report or handshake is invalid When the inter-cluster connection is established Then the protocol terminates and no application-layer communication is possible.
docs.title: ZT-70 — Refused Connection

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-071 Acceptance criterion A defined set of Harbor images can be signed via CI/CD, signatures are uploaded to Harbor, and a mock attestation is generated in JSON format. The mock attestation is generated in JSON format for any TEE vendor. Test type Technical BDD / inspection Gate G2 - Platform and documentation baseline (with BDD submission) Evidence evidence/bdd-zt-071/ Automation status pending Evidence basis none (pending) Runner godog Scenario file features/go/supply-chain.feature Given a defined set of Harbor images and the approved CI/CD signing setup When the secure-execution release workflow runs Then those images are signed, signatures are uploaded to Harbor and a JSON mock-attestation artefact is generated AND an image lacking the expected signature/attestation cannot satisfy the secure-execution gate.
docs.title: ZT-71 — Image Signing and mock Attestation

docs.text: Test ID BDD-ZT-072 Acceptance criterion OPA Gatekeeper is configured with policy and the cluster starts only properly signed images. docs.text: BDD acceptance specifications ¶ Every acceptance requirement is expressed as an executable scenario, tagged with the requirement it covers, so that traceability from requirement to test is generated rather than maintained by hand. Conventions ¶ Every Annex A row has exactly one scenario, and its Given, When and Then are the Annex wording byte for byte (see The pack ). The BDD catalogue lists them all. Each scenario carries a tag naming its requirement. Scenarios run both in CI and against live clusters. Negative cases assert against the audit entry that recorded the refusal, not merely against a failed response. The harness ¶ Two runners, one report. Go scenarios run under godog and JavaScript scenarios under Cucumber.js ; both emit the same legacy cucumber-JSON, so their results merge by concatenation and produce a single traceability sheet. Runner Scenarios Steps Report Go godog features/go/ internal/bdd/ bundles/bdd/go-report.json JavaScript Cucumber.js features/js/ features/js/steps/ bundles/bdd/js-report.json Each runner owns its own directory, and a scenario belongs to exactly one. A runner that loads the other's scenarios cannot execute their steps; it would report them as undefined and — unless the run is strict — still pass, marking those Annex rows covered by scenarios that never ran. Each runner runs three ways, and one sheet merges them: Run Scenarios Strict Go JavaScript strict implemented, not @cluster yes: an undefined or pending step fails go test ./internal/bdd npm run bdd catalogue @pending no: pending steps are expected BDD_MODE=catalogue go test ./internal/bdd npm run bdd:catalogue cluster @cluster yes — npm run bdd:cluster (needs a cluster, see below) In a pull request the cluster scenarios cannot run, so npm run bdd:cluster-dryrun lists them instead. BDD_MODE is read inside the Go test binary: unset means strict (the shared go test ./... job sets nothing), and any other value than strict or catalogue fails. go run ./cmd/bddpack -check # the pack matches the Annex GODOG_CUCUMBER_OUT=bundles/bdd/go-report.json go test ./internal/bdd # Go, strict BDD_MODE=catalogue GODOG_CUCUMBER_OUT=bundles/bdd/go-catalogue-report.json go test ./internal/bdd npm ci && npm run bdd && npm run bdd:catalogue && npm run bdd:cluster-dryrun go run ./cmd/bddreport --require-complete --rows features/annex-rows.txt --out bundles/bdd \ bundles/bdd/go-report.json bundles/bdd/js-report.json bundles/bdd/go-catalogue-report.json \ bundles/bdd/js-catalogue-report.json bundles/bdd/js-cluster-dryrun.json The pack ¶ features/annex/annex-a.json is the one source: the 94 rows of Annex A v1.7, exported once from the client's workbook (its SHA-256 is recorded), each with its statement split into Given, When and Then, its family, runner, status ( implemented or pending ) and whether it runs on a cluster. go run ./cmd/bddpack renders from it every feature file except the hand-written features/js/lifecycle.feature , the pending step definitions of both runners ( internal/bdd/pending_gen_test.go , features/js/steps/pending.gen.mjs ), features/annex-rows.txt and the catalogue . -check fails when a generated file is stale or when any feature file, hand-written or generated, departs from the Annex: a row with no scenario or two, a step that differs by one character, or a row, test-id or @pending tag above the scenario. A pending row has its Annex scenario and the tag @pending ; its steps are registered as pending (exact-text patterns, never Cucumber expressions, because many clauses contain / or ( ) ), so the row is reported as not run . Implementing a row means setting its status to implemented , writing real steps and regenerating. A clause shared by two rows stays pending until both are implemented, and the generator refuses the source otherwise. The Annex marks ZT-42/ZT-79 and ZT-46/ZT-81 as one shared execution each; each pair is one scenario carrying both rows' tags. Checks that exist but prove only part of a row — the usage manual in the site navigation (behind ZT-17), pinned and scoped workflows (behind ZT-56) — stay as untagged @regression scenarios. They run strict and do not cover a row. Cucumber.js describes its json formatter as being in maintenance mode; it is the interchange format both runners share today, and the documented upgrade path when that changes is the message format. Nothing else in the harness depends on the choice. Tags ¶ A scenario carries two tags: the requirement row it covers and the test identifier from Annex A, plus @pending while the row is not implemented and @cluster when it needs a cluster. @TDR-BDD-01 @BDD-TDR-001 Scenario: Successful deployment [fixture release] Only the row tag drives coverage. A tag shaped like a row id that matches no row in features/annex-rows.txt fails the run — a typo would otherwise leave the scenario passing while proving nothing about the row it was meant to cover. Running one Annex row ¶ BDD_MODE=catalogue go test ./internal/bdd -godog.tags=@ZT-56 # a pending Go row npm run bdd:row -- @ZT-17 # a JavaScript row, strict: # fails while ZT-17 is pending -godog.tags narrows the mode's own filter; it cannot widen a strict run to pending rows. The traceability sheet ¶ features/annex-rows.txt holds the 94 Annex A row ids in Annex order and is the denominator: the sheet reports every row, covered or not, so a gap is visible rather than absent. cmd/bddreport generates traceability.md and traceability.csv from the tags in the merged report — the sheet is never edited by hand. Covered is not proven. Each row also carries a result taken from the step and hook results of every execution that covers it: passed only when every execution passed, on every target and for every Outline example; failed when any one failed; not run when any was skipped or had no steps. A pending step counts as not run only in a scenario tagged @pending ; anywhere else it fails the row, so a stray pending step in an implemented scenario cannot hide. With --require-complete the sheet is written first, then the run fails if any row is uncovered or failed; a missing report therefore cannot pass. not run rows are complete: they are covered, and their result says they prove nothing yet. The pipeline runs all of this on every pull request, writes the sheet into the job summary, and publishes bundles/bdd as the bdd-evidence artefact, which is the per-gate evidence bundle. Scenario inventory ¶ The scenarios are grouped by the part of the architecture they exercise. Each family carries the requirements it proves and the negative case it must include — a family with no negative case is incomplete, because the demonstrator's claim is about what it refuses. Family Requirements Positive case Negative case it must include Workload identity ZT-24, ZT-57, ZT-59, ZT-60 A workload attests and receives an SVID whose SPIFFE ID matches its service account Failed attestation yields no identity and no mesh connectivity Mesh enrolment and segmentation ZT-01, ZT-23, ZT-25, ZT-26, ZT-27, ZT-58, ZT-61, ZT-62 All service traffic is routed through the mesh; only configured identities may talk An unaffiliated workload is refused, and the refusal is not IP-based Management/data plane separation ZT-49, ZT-53, ZT-55 The management plane is unreachable from the data plane A data-plane workload attempting a management-plane call is denied at the network layer Admission control ZT-02, ZT-11, ZT-12, ZT-36, ZT-37, ZT-72 A correctly signed image is admitted An unsigned or wrongly signed image is refused, with the reason code in the admission log Supply chain ZT-10, ZT-13, ZT-38, ZT-54, ZT-56, ZT-71 Images build on the runner, are signed by digest, and ship an SBOM and a mock attestation A non-Linux image, or one missing its signature, fails the pipeline Attested channel ZT-04, ZT-19, ZT-28…ZT-34, ZT-63, ZT-65…ZT-70 Both ends attest, the verdict is machine-readable, and application traffic follows A tampered measurement aborts the handshake — and it is proven no application traffic passed (ZT-70) Expected measurements and trust lists ZT-03, ZT-18, ZT-35, ZT-64 Peer digests resolve through TRAIN and match A stale or absent trust-list entry refuses the peer Authorization surface ZT-07, ZT-20, ZT-21, ZT-22, ZT-39, ZT-48, ZT-73, ZT-74, ZT-76, ZT-77, TDR-BDD-05 Dynamic registration, a token derived from a verified presentation, DPoP-bound and substituted upstream A replayed or unbound DPoP proof is rejected; a wrong scope is denied with an OID4VP link Credential lifecycle ZT-40, ZT-51 A credential is issued to the wallet and unlocks the protected resource A revoked credential flips verification negative and the token store fails closed Policy decision ZT-06, ZT-41, ZT-75 The guard permits on a matching policy and returns the resource No matching policy denies, with the rule and reason recorded Fail-secure behaviour ZT-47, ZT-52 Each request is authorised on its own merits Control-plane unavailability denies rather than admits, and raises an alert Security baseline ZT-50, TDR-BDD-07, TDR-BDD-08 TLS 1.3 and BSI TR-02102 algorithms only; credentials held in Kubernetes Secrets An older TLS version or a deprecated algorithm is rejected; no plaintext secret appears in a log Target environments ZT-14, ZT-15, TDR-BDD-10 The stack runs on each target and its Keycloak and trust endpoints respond An unsigned image is blocked on the target Release quality TDR-BDD-09, TDR-BDD-11 The release's required objects exist and are ready; helm lint and dry-run pass A chart that fails lint or dry-run cannot be promoted Visualization and journey ZT-05, ZT-08, ZT-09, ZT-43, ZT-44, ZT-45, ZT-46/ZT-81, ZT-78, ZT-80 The ORCE journey runs end to end and each step is visible Every refusal above is visible in the UI, not only in a log Documentation and reproduction ZT-16, ZT-17, ZT-42/ZT-79 Each cluster is reproduced from the environment guides alone A step that cannot be reproduced from the documentation fails the check Deployment lifecycle TDR-BDD-01…TDR-BDD-04 A release deploys, redeploys idempotently and uninstalls through ORCE Invalid parameters are refused with a machine-readable error and leave nothing behind ORCE automation QA TDR-BDD-06 — A controlled error logs a JSON record and exposes its machine-readable error in the ORCE context Final acceptance M7-01, M7-02 The approved journey is demonstrated and the final report accepted No open Critical/High release blocker at the final validation A pair written ZT-46/ZT-81 is one shared execution (one scenario, both rows). The deployment-lifecycle pack ¶ features/js/lifecycle.feature covers TDR-BDD-01..04: deploy, invalid parameters (three examples), idempotent redeploy and uninstall. features/js/orce-qa.feature covers TDR-BDD-06: a controlled error (values the chart's schema rejects) whose log record must be whole-line JSON ( ORCE logging ), carry the refusal, and contain neither the ORCE HTTP credentials nor the read token, while its machine-readable error is read from the ORCE context. Each scenario sends a command to the ORCE lifecycle workflow ( IF-08 ), reads the final result back from the ORCE context, and decides the outcome from the cluster with scripts/bdd/cluster-state.sh under a read-only identity. The scenarios are tagged @cluster : they need a cluster with ORCE and never run in a pull request. There a dry run lists them, so the traceability sheet shows their rows as covered but not run rather than as gaps. How the cluster decides ¶ Each row has its own namespace from the BDD pool ( ztd-bdd-tdr-001 .. 004 and 006 ), provisioned with ORCE by the deployment/helm/bdd-pool chart. Before a scenario the namespace must hold only its documented baseline; afterwards it is restored through the same workflow. Every object in it is classified: Class What Rule Baseline the pool's own ServiceAccount, root-CA ConfigMap, Roles and RoleBindings same set, same UIDs, throughout Helm metadata the release's helm.sh/release.v1 Secrets one per history revision, exactly one deployed Expected every top-level object the release rendered all present, ready, same UIDs across a redeploy Descendants ReplicaSets and Pods of an expected Deployment; EndpointSlices and the legacy Endpoints of an expected Service allow-list only; one active ReplicaSet, the desired Pods, endpoints that match the ready Pods and the resolved ports Events Event objects ignored Unexplained anything else must be empty — an orphan or duplicate fails the row Readiness means the rollout is complete, not that some pods are up. Every check is polled until it holds or a deadline passes (120 s by default), so asynchronous controllers are waited for; an API or authorization error fails at once and is never retried into a pass. ORCE and the observer must report the same kube-system UID, so a result can never come from another cluster. Running it ¶ Client targets run it only through CI ( bdd-cluster job, one run at a time per target; see CI/CD ). Against a developer's local cluster — never evidence: scripts/dev/kind-up.sh # kind (Kubernetes 1.35) + BDD pool + identity kubeconfigs in .dev/kind/ scripts/dev/orce-up.sh # the ORCE image on kind's network, deploying as the pool's deployer; # writes the runner inputs below to .dev/kind/orce.env set -a && . .dev/kind/orce.env && set +a npm run bdd:cluster # about 40 s; evidence in bundles/bdd/evidence/ scripts/dev/orce-down.sh && scripts/dev/kind-down.sh The ORCE image is amd64 only; on an arm64 machine Docker runs it emulated. Input Meaning KUBECONFIG the read-only observer identity BDD_ORCE_URL ORCE base URL BDD_ORCE_ADMIN_TOKEN read-only ORCE admin API bearer token BDD_ORCE_HTTP_USER , BDD_ORCE_HTTP_PASS credentials of the ORCE HTTP endpoints BDD_ORCE_LOGS_CMD a command printing the ORCE log (rows 02 and 06 assert the JSON refusal record) BDD_RELEASE_CHART the release under test, a chart path in the ORCE image; default the lifecycle fixture BDD_RELEASE_VALUES its valid baseline values; default the fixture's ci/values.yaml BDD_TARGET , BDD_RUN_ID names the target and the run in the evidence A missing input stops the run and is named. The release under test ¶ The pack deploys features/fixtures/charts/lifecycle-fixture , a namespaced chart with no CRDs, and every evidence directory records that it is fixture evidence. A fixture pass is not acceptance of the umbrella release. The umbrella chart ( deployment/helm/ztd ) is cluster-scoped: it creates the plane namespaces and a cluster role, which the pool-confined deployer cannot do. Before it may replace the fixture, those cluster-scoped deploy rights must be designed ( Umbrella chart ); it then needs its own run. Evidence ¶ Per row, target and example: bundles/bdd/evidence/bdd-tdr-00n/<target>/<example>/ holds the commands and acknowledgements, the ORCE context entry of each command (with the masked Helm output, release revision, chart digest and values hash), every classified inventory, the recorded baseline, for row 02 the refusal log record, and for row 06 the log record and a sample of the ORCE log. Traceability ¶ Each scenario's tag is its requirement id, so the requirement-to-test matrix is generated from the feature files rather than maintained beside them. A requirement with no tagged scenario shows up as a gap in that matrix; that is the point of generating it. Evidence ¶ Each gate produces one indexed evidence bundle, assembled by a single command, with a directory per requirement row. Bundles are versioned and immutable once a gate has consumed them.
